source.title: APEX: Probing Neural Networks via Activation Perturbation
source.authors: Tao Ren; Xiao-Yu Luo; Qiong-Xiu Li

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendices, is present; no apparent truncation.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own results about activation-noise stability, random-label training, and sample-regularity scores, but it does not test the generalization behaviors specified in V1–V8. It neither measures the training–test generalization gap nor tests the named interventions or magnitude-aware sharpness measure.
record.gate_note: The paper varies random-label ratios and measures escape noise, and relates escape noise to memorization and consistency scores. It does not report the natural-label versus random-label test-accuracy comparison in V1, test error versus width in V2, or any other version's specified outcome. Those nearby measurements are recorded under fits_no_version. Other results, including backdoor target-class concentration, do not bear on these claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures inference-time prediction stability and representation structure. It reports neither the training and held-out accuracy comparison required by V1 nor the interventions and outcomes required by V2–V8. Its parameter perturbations are uniform additive noise, not magnitude-aware sharpness, and are not compared with generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors present APEX as an inference-time probe connecting local sample regularity, semantic prediction transitions, and global training-induced biases, including backdoor target alignment. They do not establish that escape noise tracks training–test generalization gaps.
record.recipe_differences: Inference-time activation perturbation and escape-noise measurement; the listed versions concern training outcomes, interventions, or generalization measures.
record.method_sensitivity: The measured escape-noise trend with random-label ratio is reported for multiple dataset–architecture pairs. Input and parameter perturbations do not show a consistent monotonic decrease in the reported ablations.

fits_no_version.finding: Average escape noise decreases with increasing random-label ratios for ResNet-18 and DenseNet on CIFAR-10 and VGG-11 on GTSRB. Input and parameter perturbations show no consistent monotonic decrease.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation escape noise detects training-induced differences in local prediction stability under label randomization.

fits_no_version.finding: On ImageNet and CIFAR-100, samples with higher consistency scores or lower memorization scores tolerate larger activation perturbations before their predictions become unstable.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Activation escape noise aligns with established sample-level regularity scores.

record.problems: The claim-relevant generalization outcomes are not measured. The random-label and regularity-score results are shown in figures without reported numeric values or uncertainty estimates in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No reported results were omitted for the claim versions. Other paper results, including semantic transitions, large-noise stationarity, backdoor target-class concentration, and robustness to noise type or layer choice, do not measure outcomes named by V1–V8.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels together with above-chance natural-label held-out accuracy and chance random-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe.
Training and test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Held-out performance of convolutional versus fully connected networks, including local connectivity and initialization effects.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out performance under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Effects of training-time dropout on held-out error, including dataset size, dropout strength, and augmentation.
Association between magnitude-aware weight sharpness and training–test gaps, including comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy changes after removing highly memorized training examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text supports the extracted qualitative trends. States are cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because none of these rows measures a version's effect; this does not dispute the escape-noise findings. No claim-relevant omitted result was found.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare natural-label and random-label test accuracy, or report whether random-label training reaches near-zero training error.
Does not sweep network width against training and test error.
Does not compare convolutional and fully connected networks on test error.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out performance.
Does not compare batch sizes on held-out performance.
Does not evaluate dropout effects on held-out error.
Does not measure magnitude-aware sharpness or compare it with the training–test generalization gap.
Does not remove memorized training examples and measure the resulting test accuracy.

rows.measure: Relationship between escape noise and regularity scores
rows.value: strong correlations with both metrics; exact correlation values not stated in text
rows.note: Text describes strong correlations and says samples with high C-scores and low memorization scores have large escape-noise values; exact values are not given.
rows.check: The reported correlations concern sample regularity, not the test-accuracy effect of removing memorized examples. Split by dataset and score; escape noise increases with consistency score and decreases with memorization score. Section 4.3 identifies ResNet-50 models but specifies Inception-based CIFAR-100 consistency scores.
